purpose: Harden empirical sources, separate intervention classes and audit whether current AI-dependence/companion literature can support claims across sexual-orientation and gender-diverse populations.

source_registry.title: Addicted, attached, or just delegating? A scoping review on problematic artificial intelligence use
source_registry.risk_of_bias_note: Formal methodological quality assessment was not the purpose of the scoping review; the literature is dominated by heterogeneous constructs and many cross-sectional studies.
source_registry.independence_note: Treat as a map of primary studies, not 37 automatically independent confirmations of one construct.
source_registry.claim_use: Field-level evidence that dependence constructs and samples are heterogeneous; insufficient for SOGI-specific coefficients.

source_registry.title: A scoping review on the mental health harms of LLM-based chatbots
source_registry.scope: 36 articles in AI-dependence strand; predominantly cross-sectional/qualitative with only one longitudinal correlational and one experimental study
source_registry.risk_of_bias_note: Heterogeneous definitions and measurement tools; dependence measures are often adapted from other technology-addiction scales or self-developed.
source_registry.claim_use: Supports the need for measurement harmonization before subgroup calibration.

source_registry.title: Generative artificial intelligence dependency: Scale development, validation, and its motivational, behavioral, and psychological correlates
source_registry.sample: N=1333 total, United States and Singapore
source_registry.effect_or_quality: alpha .92-.93; test-retest ICC .87; scalar measurement invariance across male/female sex and cultures
source_registry.sogi_limit: Measurement invariance was established only for male versus female sex categories; accessible report does not establish sexual-orientation, TGD, nonbinary or intersex invariance.
source_registry.risk_of_bias_note: Self-report; younger/tech-savvy samples; some development studies did not formally collect demographics.
source_registry.claim_use: Strong general psychometric anchor but not SOGI-validated dependence measurement.

source_registry.title: Problematic ChatGPT Use Scale: AI-Human Collaboration or Unraveling the Dark Side of ChatGPT
source_registry.sample: Study I N=391, 61.4% female; Study II N=473, 74.4% male; Türkiye
source_registry.sogi_limit: No verified SOGI-diverse subgroup validation in accessible report.
source_registry.claim_use: Psychometric/problematic-use bridge; does not establish fairness across sexual/gender-diverse groups.

source_registry.title: Connecting self-esteem to problematic AI chatbot use: the multiple mediating roles of positive and negative psychological states
source_registry.claim_use: Direct problematic-AI-use evidence, but SOGI representativeness is unresolved.

source_registry.title: Loneliness and AI chatbot dependence in young adults: the mediating role of perceived social support
source_registry.sogi_limit: No sexual-orientation or transgender fields were located in the accessible article text.
source_registry.risk_of_bias_note: Cross-sectional convenience/self-report design; mediation is statistical, not temporal causation.
source_registry.claim_use: Strong association anchor; not transportable to SOGI subgroups.

source_registry.title: Depression and the use of conversational AI for companionship among college students
source_registry.sogi_limit: Gender moderation was tested as a binary category; no verified sexual-orientation/TGD subgroup analysis in accessible report.
source_registry.claim_use: Companionship-use mechanism evidence, not inclusive dependence calibration.

source_registry.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence in the Lives of Young Adults: Exploring Motivations and Mental Health
source_registry.sample: N=1003 US young adults ages 18-25; 56.3% women, 39.4% men, 4.3% another gender
source_registry.sogi_limit: Accessible abstract reports an another-gender category and gender comparisons, but does not establish dependence-scale invariance or sexual-orientation-specific dependence effects.
source_registry.claim_use: Useful bridge showing that nonbinary/other-gender participants can be represented in GenAI research; not a dependence validation study.

source_registry.title: Loneliness and generative AI use for companionship among college students
source_registry.sample: N=858 US college students; 17% reported AI companionship use
source_registry.sogi_result: LGBQ+ students were less likely to report AI companionship use; accessible abstract does not provide a transportable LGBQ+ dependence effect size.
source_registry.risk_of_bias_note: Cross-sectional; companionship use is not dependence or impairment.
source_registry.claim_use: First direct SOGI x companionship-use signal in this P0.2 audit.

source_registry.title: Clinical and sociodemographic predictors of AI use for mental health among college students
source_registry.sample: AI module n=896; analytic N=675 across two US institutions
source_registry.sogi_result: Never-use-AI group contained higher proportions of nonbinary/other gender and LGBQ+ students; study explicitly analyzed gender and sexual orientation.
source_registry.risk_of_bias_note: Cross-sectional; two institutions; overall HMS response rate reported as 8%; AI-for-mental-health use is not dependence.
source_registry.independence_note: Shares Healthy Minds Study 2024-2025 infrastructure with P02S009; participant overlap must be checked before counting as independent SOGI replication.
source_registry.claim_use: Strong representation audit anchor, not dependence-effect evidence.

source_registry.title: A socially assistive robot to support mental wellbeing in LGBTQ+ young people at risk of self-harm: a randomized controlled trial
source_registry.sample: Final analytic N=153 UK LGBTQ+ youth ages 16-25; 49.7% cisgender, 50.3% transgender or gender-diverse
source_registry.heterogeneity_result: Primary benefit was significant in cisgender participants but not TGD participants in post-hoc interaction probing; anxiety showed a similar interaction pattern.
source_registry.risk_of_bias_note: Not an LLM or chatbot; self-selection toward a comforting robotic device is possible; gender-interaction analyses were added after protocol publication but prespecified before data analysis; differential survey-response decline occurred by condition.
source_registry.claim_use: High-value proof that aggregate AI-support effects may hide gender-identity heterogeneity; no coefficient transfer to LLM dependence.

source_registry.title: Enhancing LGBTQ+ Inclusivity in an AI-Powered Sexual Health Chatbot
source_registry.sample: Youth Advisory Council N=15 LGBTQ+ teenagers
source_registry.key_result: Participants identified limitations in transgender-specific content, inclusivity, tone, conversational depth and stigma reduction.
source_registry.risk_of_bias_note: Small qualitative co-design sample; no efficacy or dependence outcome.
source_registry.claim_use: Direct evidence that inclusive content quality requires dedicated evaluation; not a risk/dependence coefficient.

source_registry.title: Conversational artificial intelligence interventions to support smoking cessation: a systematic review and meta-analysis
source_registry.sample: 5 RCTs, combined N=58,796; meta-analysis of 3 trials
source_registry.risk_of_bias_note: Overall risk of bias high, loss to follow-up generally high, interventions heterogeneous; effect sensitive to study exclusion.
source_registry.claim_use: D011 nicotine receives direct therapeutic conversational-agent evidence, but this cannot be treated as an LLM companion effect.

source_registry.title: Effectiveness and Acceptability of Conversational Agents for Smoking Cessation: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
source_registry.risk_of_bias_note: Mixed study quality; publication-bias signal; heterogeneity in agents and outcomes.
source_registry.independence_note: Overlaps substantially in topic/trials with P02S013; do not count both meta-analyses as independent primary evidence.

source_registry.title: The Effect of Chatbot Interventions on Gambling Disorder: A Systematic Review
source_registry.key_result: Within-group gambling reductions occurred, but between-group differences were often nonsignificant; evidence base remains scarce.
source_registry.risk_of_bias_note: Only two eligible trials; insufficient replication depth.
source_registry.claim_use: D017 gambling upgraded from unknown to direct therapeutic-chatbot evidence with weak/limited comparative efficacy.

source_registry.title: Unguided Chatbot-Delivered Cognitive Behavioural Intervention for Problem Gamblers Through Messaging App
source_registry.risk_of_bias_note: Primary endpoint not significant; secondary endpoint significant; messaging-app CBT chatbot, not modern LLM.

source_registry.title: Guided versus unguided chatbot-delivered cognitive behavioral intervention for moderate-risk and problem gambling: GAMBOT2
source_registry.risk_of_bias_note: Both arms received chatbot CBT, so trial isolates added therapist support rather than chatbot versus no chatbot.
source_registry.independence_note: Same GAMBOT intervention lineage as P02S016; separate sample but not independent platform replication.
source_registry.claim_use: Shows no additional therapist-guidance effect; preserves chatbot efficacy uncertainty.

source_registry.title: Investigating AI Chatbot Dependence: Associations with Internet and Smartphone Dependence, Mental Health Outcomes, and the Moderating Role of Usage Purposes
source_registry.key_result: AI chatbot dependence was moderately correlated with internet and smartphone dependence; depression/anxiety associations were positive, well-being association was not direct.
source_registry.risk_of_bias_note: Cross-sectional; association cannot establish smartphone/internet dependence as a cause of AI dependence.
source_registry.claim_use: D022 problematic-smartphone lane upgraded to direct associational bridge with AI chatbot dependence; no causal coefficient.

source_independence_graph.rule: Do not count as independent replication until participant/institution overlap is resolved.
Meta-analyses overlap in intervention literature and must not be summed as separate primary trials.
Separate randomized samples, same intervention lineage; replication is partial, not platform-independent.

dependency_updates.name: NICOTINE_TOBACCO
dependency_updates.claim_ceiling: Conversational-agent cessation interventions can improve cessation outcomes in some settings; do not infer that companion/general LLM use reduces or increases nicotine dependence.

dependency_updates.name: GAMBLING
dependency_updates.claim_ceiling: Chatbot CBT is feasible and may improve some gambling outcomes, but robust comparative efficacy is not established and evidence is based on very few trials.

dependency_updates.name: PROBLEMATIC_SMARTPHONE_USE
dependency_updates.claim_ceiling: Smartphone dependence and AI chatbot dependence co-vary; no temporal or causal direction established.

dependency_updates.name: PROBLEMATIC_SOCIAL_MEDIA_USE
dependency_updates.claim_ceiling: Keep as shared-risk/mechanism hypothesis until direct peer-reviewed intersection evidence is extracted.
No coefficient transport from mixed-SUD or neighboring classes.

sogi_representativeness_audit.audit_scope: Core direct AI-dependence/problematic-use studies plus adjacent AI-companionship/mental-health studies surfaced in P0.2; not a claim of exhaustive coverage of every AI paper.
sogi_representativeness_audit.direct_dependence_core_pattern: Most hardened direct dependence/problematic-use studies in this pass report binary male/female sex or gender categories; inclusive SOGI measurement and subgroup psychometric invariance are largely absent.
sogi_representativeness_audit.direct_sogi_ai_use_signal: Healthy Minds AI studies explicitly measured LGBQ+ and nonbinary/other gender, but outcomes were companionship or mental-health AI use rather than dependence/impairment.
sogi_representativeness_audit.targeted_sogi_intervention_signal: Dedicated LGBTQ+ AI-adjacent intervention/co-design studies exist, including an RCT with 50.3% TGD participants, but they study mental wellbeing or inclusive information delivery rather than LLM dependence.
sogi_representativeness_audit.intersex_status: No direct AI-dependence intersex/variation-in-sex-characteristics analysis was hardened in this pass.
sogi_representativeness_audit.asexual_pansexual_specificity: No direct dependence-effect estimates for asexual, pansexual or other specific orientation groups were hardened in this pass; aggregation into LGBQ+ can conceal heterogeneity.
sogi_representativeness_audit.trans_nonbinary_measurement_invariance: No direct AI-dependence scale in this hardened set established measurement invariance specifically across cisgender versus transgender/nonbinary groups.
sogi_representativeness_audit.main_gap: The field contains some inclusive AI-use and LGBTQ-targeted research, but the validated AI-dependence measurement literature remains substantially less representative than the broader AI-use literature.

topa_kills: Kill the claim that male/female measurement invariance proves gender-diverse validity.
Kill the claim that an LGBTQ-targeted AI intervention proves LGBTQ-specific AI-dependence risk or protection.
Kill the claim that lower LGBQ+ companionship use implies lower dependence risk.
Kill the claim that nonbinary/other-gender representation alone proves psychometric equivalence.
Kill double counting of Healthy Minds, smoking-meta and GAMBOT lineages as independent replication.
Kill transport of legacy therapeutic chatbot efficacy to modern general-purpose or companion LLMs.
p0_3_required: Extract exact sex/gender/orientation variables from every one of the 37 primary studies in the Dagnino review where full text permits.
Build a study-by-study SOGI reporting matrix with NOT_REPORTED as an explicit state.
Check whether any AI-dependence scale includes nonbinary/TGD participants and testable cell sizes; request or use public datasets when available.

Pre-register measurement-invariance tests for cisgender/TGD and heterosexual/LGBQ+ only where cell sizes and construct validity support them; never force sparse identities into unstable significance tests.
Separate sex assigned at birth from gender identity in future data collection.
Preserve open self-description and suppress sparse cells for privacy.
Continue D/N dependency-card source hardening without weakening SOGI privacy rules.
seal: REPRESENTATION IS DATA QUALITY. IDENTITY IS NOT A DEPENDENCE COEFFICIENT.
